rationale: A coherent, sign-consistent pairing of the archive's two strongest legs (asset-side accrual numerator, cash-to-liabilities constraint) that is not itself in the archive, though it remains an interpolation between two validated parents and `che` still enters both legs, so a modest gain over `ConstrainedFirmAccrualPricing` would be uninformative about whether the interaction adds anything.

The non-cash-current-asset ("least reliable accrual") decomposition scaled by activity and conditioned on profitability is essentially the Richardson-Sloan-Soliman-Tuna accrual-reliability result, and relative to the archive it changes only the deflator of `AssetSideUnfundedAccrual`, making it a clean ablation but a low-information one to spend a slot on.

The accrual × leverage/distress interaction is close to published accrual-distress conditioning, and `lt/ceq` is a badly behaved conditioner because negative or near-zero book equity — precisely the most fragile firms the hypothesis targets — produces negative or explosive ratios that rank at the wrong end, so a weak result would not cleanly distinguish leverage from liquidity as the hypothesis claims.

The expression does not compute the stated mechanism — `NEG(ABS(ni/sale))` weights small losses identically to the small *profits* that the benchmark-beating story is about, and it also loads on low-profitability firms generally, directly opposing the archive's validated finding that accruals are most informative among persistently profitable and high-gross-profit firms; an asymmetric small-positive-margin indicator would test the hypothesis properly.

This is a deflator rescaling of an existing archive primitive rather than a new mechanism, and `ceq` is the weakest of the available scalers because negative and near-zero book equity flips signs and generates extreme values that winsorization will crudely truncate, so the test is unlikely to resolve anything economically.

Genuinely combines two economically distinct and separately validated legs — asset-side unfunded accrual capacity and the margin-decline incentive — with a consistent sign and no shared inputs, so a joint improvement would be attributable to the interaction rather than to redundancy, with the only caveat being deflator instability when `MA(che,3)` is near zero.
